questions.prompt: How does a Stream differ from Pub/Sub?

options.text: A Stream persists its entries so they can be replayed by ID; Pub/Sub stores nothing
A Stream delivers to every subscriber; Pub/Sub delivers to one
A Stream cannot have more than one consumer
There is no real difference

questions.explanation: Streams are an append-only, persistent log — entries stay and can be re-read by ID. Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget with no history.

questions.prompt: What does passing `*` as the ID to XADD do?

options.text: Deletes the oldest entry
Tells Redis to auto-generate the next (increasing) entry ID
Reads all entries
Acknowledges the entry

questions.explanation: `*` asks Redis to generate the next ID (a millisecond timestamp plus a sequence number), keeping the stream strictly ordered.

questions.prompt: Which statements about consumer groups are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Each entry is delivered to one consumer in the group, not all of them
An unacknowledged entry stays in the Pending Entries List (PEL)
XACK removes an entry from the PEL
Entries are automatically deleted from the stream once acknowledged

questions.explanation: Consumer groups split work, track unacked entries in the PEL, and clear them with XACK. XACK does NOT delete the entry from the stream itself — trimming (MAXLEN/XTRIM) does that.

questions.prompt: A consumer reads an entry with XREADGROUP but crashes before acknowledging it. What happens?

options.text: The entry is lost permanently
The entry stays in the PEL and can be reclaimed by another consumer via XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM
The whole stream is rolled back
The entry is delivered to every other consumer immediately

questions.explanation: Because delivery is at-least-once, the unacknowledged entry remains pending and another consumer can claim and finish it — nothing is silently lost.

questions.prompt: The command a consumer runs to acknowledge that it finished processing a stream entry is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: XACK marks an entry as processed and removes it from the group's Pending Entries List.

questions.prompt: How do you keep a busy stream from consuming memory without bound?

options.text: It trims itself automatically
Cap it with MAXLEN on XADD (e.g. MAXLEN ~ 10000) or trim with XTRIM
Call XACK on every entry
Streams never use memory

questions.explanation: Streams persist, so you must bound them explicitly with MAXLEN (the ~ makes trimming approximate and cheaper) or XTRIM. XACK only clears the PEL, not the log.
